claim: Average percent effective spreads of at-the-money SPX 0DTE options were 8.7% of the option price for calls and 9.5% for puts, against about 6% for 1–6-day options and about 2% for options with 42–48 days left, in OPRA trade data from January 2004 to July 2021 (Doshi, Pederzoli & Sert, 2025 working paper).

evidence.quote: The average spread is very high, ranging from a maximum of 9% for 0DTE options to a minimum of 2% for options with 21-48 days to maturity.

claim: Option bid-ask spreads follow a U-shape through the trading day, widest at the open and the close.

evidence.quote: bid-ask spread follows a U-shaped pattern over the trading day, widening at the open and close

claim: VIX1D is computed in business minutes on a 405-minute trading day. Its weight shifts from same-day to next-day SPX options as the session goes on, and from about 3:00 p.m. ET the same-day component is frozen at its last valid value.

evidence.quote: The calculation of the VIX1D Index uses business years and business minutes – this is a different increment than the VIX Index, which uses calendar years and calendar minutes.

when the time to expiration for the near-term (current day expiry) series is less than 60 business minutes (approximately 3:00 p.m. ET), the single-term volatility of the near term will be the last valid value

claim: In Beckmeyer, Branger & Gayda's retail data, the average retail long SPX 0DTE position lost 53% of its value over the full sample and 61% since May 2022, while short positions earned 48% and 56%.

evidence.quote: While the average long position of retail investors lost 53% of its value across the full sample and 61% for the sample since May 2022, selling insurance earned a large premium for the average trade, with returns of 48% and 56%, respectively.

claim: Vilkov finds a positive but economically tiny variance risk premium in SPX 0DTE options (Sept 2016–Jan 2024, positions opened at 10:00 and held to the close), and no unhedged structure held to expiry was consistently profitable.

evidence.quote: Only risk reversals - long call, short put - produced slightly positive mean returns, roughly 0.01% of the index value , trivial even before costs.
implied volatility tends to be high relative to what is subsequently realized, even at same-day horizons.
